name: Sushumna
quality: Neutral, luminous, the path of ascent
course: From Muladhara at the base of the spine straight up through every chakra to the crown (Brahmarandhra).
description: The hero channel. Hatha and Tantric texts describe it running inside the spinal column; Kundalini is said to rise through it. Later texts describe finer channels within it — Vajrā, within that Citriṇī, and innermost the Brahma-nāḍī.
practice: Feel a fine line of light along the spine. With the breath balanced between both nostrils, rest attention on that central line.

name: Ida
course: Begins at Muladhara, spirals around Sushumna crossing it at each chakra, and ends at the left nostril, meeting the others at Ajna.
description: The left, lunar current. Associated with coolness, rest and inward attention, and traditionally with breath through the left nostril.
practice: Breathing gently through the left nostril is traditionally said to favour Ida.

name: Pingala
course: Begins at Muladhara, spirals around Sushumna opposite to Ida, crossing at each chakra, and ends at the right nostril, meeting the others at Ajna.
description: The right, solar current. Associated with warmth, activity and outward attention, and traditionally with breath through the right nostril.
practice: Breathing gently through the right nostril is traditionally said to favour Pingala.
